required_documents.name: SF-424 Application for Federal Assistance
required_documents.details: Standard application cover sheet submitted through Grants.gov workspace.

required_documents.name: 36-Month ADPI Project Narrative
required_documents.details: Detailed narrative outlining 36-month cooperative agreement plan to expand dementia-capable home and community-based service (HCBS) systems under Option A (Grants to States) or Option B (Grants to Communities).

required_documents.name: Option A State Agency Designation or Option B Community Provider Certification
required_documents.details: For Option A: Documentation establishing applicant as governmental entity with lead responsibility for aging and Alzheimer services in the State (one per state). For Option B: Proof of community HCBS service delivery.

required_documents.name: SF-424A Budget Information and 36-Month Budget Narrative
required_documents.details: Budget breakdown requesting up to ,000,000 total federal funding across the 36-month project period with required matching funds.

required_documents.name: Dementia-Capable HCBS Partner Letters of Commitment
required_documents.details: Letters of commitment from health systems, community agencies, caregiver support organizations, and aging service networks.

required_documents.name: SAM.gov Active UEI and Grants.gov Workspace Credentials
required_documents.details: Active registration on SAM.gov with Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and authorized organizational representative on Grants.gov.

eligibility.summary: Option A: State governments (lead agency for aging/Alzheimer services; only one per state). Option B: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, county and city governments, public higher education institutions, and tribal organizations. Foreign entities are ineligible.

cost_share.details: Non-federal matching funds required (minimum 25% non-federal match per Older Americans Act Title IV guidelines).

review_criteria.criterion: Quality of Dementia-Capable System Expansion & Strengths-Based Services
Community Needs Assessment and Engagement of Caregivers & Individuals with Dementia
Priority consideration for providers not funded under ADI-SSS/ADPI since before 2014

funded_activities.activity: Expanding dementia-capable home and community-based services (HCBS) to help people living with dementia remain safely at home.
Implementing evidence-based caregiver training, respite support, and behavioral symptom management interventions.
Dementia screening, early detection protocols, and specialized professional training for healthcare and social service providers.

submission_limits: No entity is eligible to apply for both State and Community options, and no entity may hold more than one ADPI grant at a time.
important_notes: Cooperative agreements funded under 36-month awards up to ,000,000.
State applicants (Option A) must coordinate directly with the North Carolina Division of Aging and Adult Services.
